summary: Documents a Cisco mechanism for isolating devices with special Layer 2 forwarding rules, so that devices can share one IP subnet while being isolated from each other. This lets designers use larger subnets and reduce the address management overhead.

eli5.summary: In an apartment building everyone shares the hallway, but each flat stays closed. Private VLANs let computers share one network address range while being kept apart from each other.

subtitle: Isolate servers and devices while sharing one subnet and conserving VLAN IDs.

tldr.problem: A web hosting provider or metropolitan Ethernet service wants to separate hundreds of customer servers for security but faces a VLAN scalability ceiling: IEEE 802.1Q supports only 4094 VLANs. Assigning one VLAN per customer quickly exhausts this limit. Each VLAN also wastes IP addresses because it requires its own subnet.
tldr.mechanism: Private VLANs partition a single primary VLAN into smaller isolated or community sub-domains by assigning special designations to switch ports. Isolated ports prevent their endpoints from talking to each other at Layer 2. Community ports allow endpoints within a community to talk to each other and to trusted gateways (promiscuous ports) but not to other communities. VLAN ID pairing allows two VLAN IDs to enforce these constraints.
tldr.outcome: Service providers can isolate hundreds of customers with just two VLAN IDs, reduce IP address waste, and allow customers to share one subnet while being Layer 2 isolated from each other.

today: RFC 5517 documents a vendor-specific feature from Cisco Systems. Private VLANs remain widely used in data centers, hosting environments, and metropolitan Ethernet services. The architecture is a de facto standard supported by multiple switch vendors, though implementations vary in detail and multi-vendor interoperability requires careful planning.

sections.title: The VLAN Scalability Problem
sections.content:
In traditional Ethernet networks, a VLAN is a broadcast domain where hosts can establish direct Layer 2 communication. If untrusted devices share a VLAN, security problems arise: one host can listen to broadcasts from others, learn their MAC addresses, and establish direct Layer 2 communication bypassing firewalls.

The traditional solution is to assign a separate VLAN to each security domain. However, IEEE 802.1Q limits VLAN IDs to a 12-bit field, allowing only 4094 usable VLANs (IDs 0 and 4095 are reserved). A web hosting provider with 4000 customer servers would need 4000 VLANs, exceeding this limit. Even with fewer customers, each VLAN requires its own subnet, wasting IP addresses on network infrastructure (subnet address, broadcast address, gateway addresses) rather than allocating them to customer hosts.

Private VLANs solve both problems by allowing multiple customers to share one primary VLAN while being Layer 2 isolated from each other.
sections.eli5: One VLAN per customer uses too many VLAN IDs and wastes IP addresses. Private VLANs let many customers fit in just a couple of VLAN IDs while staying separated from each other.

sections.title: Private VLAN Architecture: Ports and Domains
sections.content:
A private VLAN domain consists of a single primary VLAN (Vp) paired with one or more secondary VLANs (Vs). Secondary VLANs can be isolated VLANs (Vi) or community VLANs (Vc). The pairing uses just two VLAN IDs total: one primary and (usually) one isolated, plus zero or more community VLANs.

Three port designations enforce Layer 2 isolation rules. An isolated port connects a customer device that should not communicate with other isolated ports. The device can reach promiscuous ports (such as a gateway router) but not other isolated devices. A community port belongs to a named group; ports within one community can talk to each other and to promiscuous ports, but cannot reach other communities or isolated ports. A promiscuous port can communicate with any other port type and is typically used for gateways, DHCP servers, and management stations.

For example, a hosting provider assigns isolated ports to untrusted customer servers. A customer with multiple related servers uses community ports so the servers can talk to each other. A router and DHCP server connect via promiscuous ports, allowing all customers to reach them.
sections.eli5: Isolated ports keep servers away from each other. Community ports let a group of servers talk to each other. Promiscuous ports let the router and servers talk to everyone. All share the same primary VLAN and subnet.

sections.title: VLAN Pairing and Port Characteristics
sections.content:
Enforcement of private VLAN isolation rules requires VLAN ID pairs. A primary VLAN (Vp) is the shared VLAN ID for all endpoints and services in the domain. An isolated VLAN (Vi) is a secondary VLAN whose ports are all isolated from each other; frames tagged with Vi between isolated ports are blocked. A community VLAN (Vc) allows ports to communicate within the community; frames tagged with Vc between community ports within the same group are allowed.

Promiscuous ports are configured with the primary VLAN and all secondary VLANs, so they appear in both the primary VLAN and the isolation/community domains. Isolated and community ports are configured with the primary VLAN for communication with promiscuous ports, and with their respective secondary VLAN for isolation logic.

The scheme requires only standard IEEE 802.1Q tagging with at most a single VLAN tag per frame; no double-tagging is needed. Inter-switch link ports (trunk ports) carry frames from multiple VLANs, including the primary and secondary, maintaining isolation behavior consistently across multiple switches in a Layer 2 network.
sections.eli5: Each pair of VLAN IDs represents a private VLAN domain. One ID is primary (everyone's subnet), the other is secondary (isolation rules). All frames have one tag, not two.

sections.title: Flexible IP Address Allocation
sections.content:
In a traditional multi-VLAN design, each VLAN requires its own subnet, wasting address space. In a private VLAN domain, all members of the primary VLAN share a common subnet. An end device can be assigned an IP address statically or via DHCP from a server connected to a promiscuous port.

Since addresses are allocated from a shared pool rather than subdivided into smaller per-VLAN subnets, fewer addresses are reserved for infrastructure. Administrators have greater flexibility in assigning and reassigning addresses as customers grow or shrink. This is particularly valuable in large hosting environments with hundreds of customers.
sections.eli5: All computers in a private VLAN domain share one big subnet and one pool of addresses. There is less waste than giving each customer their own subnet, so more addresses are available for actual computers.

sections.title: Routing Behavior and Security Implications
sections.content:
Private VLANs confine isolation rules to Layer 2. Layer 3 entities (routers) see only the primary VLAN and are unaware of secondary VLAN structure. Two isolated devices in the same subnet can communicate at Layer 3 via the router because the router assumes same-subnet hosts should be able to reach each other.

To enable Layer 2-isolated endpoints to communicate at Layer 3, routers connected to promiscuous ports MUST support a proxy-ARP-like function. When an isolated host on the router's subnet tries to reach another isolated host, the router intercepts the ARP request, responds on behalf of the destination, and then routes the IP packet normally.

When a private VLAN spans multiple switches, inter-switch link ports carry frames from all VLAN IDs and maintain the isolation behavior: traffic from an isolated port in one switch does not reach isolated or community ports in another switch. This requires switches in a multi-vendor network to support the private VLAN feature; switches that do not understand the secondary VLAN structure may violate isolation rules, flooding unicast frames across isolation boundaries.

If properly deployed, private VLANs effectively constrain Layer 2 forwarding to block ARP poisoning, port scanning, and other attacks that depend on direct Layer 2 access.
sections.eli5: Routers still see one big subnet, so two isolated computers can reach each other through the router using IP (not Layer 2). On multi-switch networks, all switches must understand private VLANs or isolation breaks. Private VLANs block Layer 2 attacks like ARP spoofing.
